headline: High: gpt-researcher can ingest and emit untrusted research content while pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-service runtime can propagate it into downstream actions or third-party APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web/files and can call MCP, so attacker-controlled content can enter its outputs; pipecat consumes text on a shared bus and can route it into LLM/transport services. The bridge is plausible by default, but not directly documented as an instruction parser hijack, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher fetches untrusted pages and emits them as plain text instructions
IF pipecat routes shared-bus text into an LLM or agent prompt without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all gpt-researcher outputs
Strip imperative phrases before handing text to pipecat
Route only structured summaries between agents
Disable shared-bus fanout for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add prompt-firewall validation

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and secrets like API keys, while pipecat processes text/conversation state and can send data to multiple external STT/LLM/TTS APIs. A shared workspace or bus could leak sensitive research material into third-party inference, but the profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace or message bus
IF gpt-researcher loads local documents containing secrets or sensitive research
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Remove secrets from gpt-researcher inputs
Disable external API services in pipecat for sensitive runs
Use redaction before any handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, install packages, and use broad network egress; pipecat has allowlisted egress and shared-bus concurrency. Their overlapping mutable surfaces create coordination risk, but the profiles do not show both writing the same directory or git state, so this is conflict-prone but not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable project directory
IF pipecat instances share a bus while gpt-researcher writes artifacts into that bus-backed workspace
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Freeze package installs during shared runs
Serialize access to shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add locking around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can generate research claims and citations, and pipecat can consume text and drive downstream LLM, transport, or video services. If pipecat treats gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions or user-facing speech, making the default pathway dangerous.
conditions: IF pipecat forwards gpt-researcher output into an action-taking service
IF no verification step checks citations or factual claims before downstream use
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actioning outputs
Require citation verification on all claims
Limit pipecat to read-only presentation mode
Log and diff source text before reuse
requires-engineering: add automated fact-check gates

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs, while pipecat can route text, audio, video, and analytics to many third-party services. The pair can therefore move regulated content across vendors with different retention or residency terms, but the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF pipecat is configured to use external STT/LLM/TTS or analytics providers
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pair
Choose vendors with matching residency terms
Disable analytics exports
Document retention settings for each service
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
